The size of the tube is usually determined according to the size of the tyre for which it is intended, and therefore the marking of the tube will be identical to the marking of the tyre. The "X" mark usually links the overall external diameter (D) and the width (B). The "-" mark usually links the width (B) and the rim diameter (d). In bicycle tyres, it is customary to mark the tyre as follows: a tyre with dimensions 26X200 should be interpreted as D X B; i.e., the overall external diameter is 26", and the tyre width is 2".

The size of the tube is usually determined according to the size of the tyre for which it is intended, and therefore the marking of the tube will be identical to the marking of the tyre.
